question: Can the exact SAW3 interval spanning the shared 00:51:15.947 UTC crew report be materialized within a 64 MiB client-side media budget by using smaller range responses?
terminal_objective: Determine whether released overlapping pixels can tighten the flash receipt without downloading the 2.96 GB source or treating timing overlap as event capture.
baseline: Stage 5A verified byte-range support but exhausted 64 MiB after allowing 32 MiB proxy responses; no clip was materialized.
treatment: Repeat the same exact channel and 15-second interval with one-MiB maximum proxy responses and a 64-KiB container probe.
authority: Private bounded source acquisition and local inspection only. No publication, impact confirmation, photometric claim, full-product download, second-channel widening, or outreach.
claim_ceiling: A passing transport canary establishes only that the exact label-timed interval was materialized. Pixel inspection must separately establish whether the Moon is visible and whether any transient is present. Neither timing overlap nor a visible transient independently establishes impact causation, geolocation, photometry, or a mapping to an annotated event.

next_step_logic.on_success: Inspect the exact clip for target visibility and transient candidates under a separate content receipt.
next_step_logic.on_budget_stop: Preserve the result and retain the overlapping stream as unvalidated coverage unless an exact sample-table route becomes cheaper.
next_step_logic.on_target_not_visible: Record the overlap as non-informative camera coverage and do not inspect channel 2 automatically.
next_step_logic.on_candidate: Require frame-level timing, persistence, artifact rejection, lunar localization, and independent evidence before changing the flash claim.
next_step_logic.stop: Do not download the complete source or widen to another source without a decision-changing reason.
